test_title: PYST 44: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 16 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements is FALSE regarding cells?

options.text: Cells can be round, oval, spindle-shaped or branched.
All cells are of the same size and shape.
Nerve cells are long to help in the conduction of impulses.
Cell shape is often related to its function.

solution:
The correct answer is __**All cells are of the same size and shape.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cells can be round, oval, spindle-shaped, or branched:** The shape of cells varies significantly depending on their type and function. For instance, red blood cells are biconcave, while nerve cells are elongated. *This statement is correct.*
 
• **All cells are of the same size and shape:** This is a false statement. Cells vary greatly in size and shape based on their role in the body. For example, a human egg cell is much larger than a red blood cell, and nerve cells are elongated to transmit signals efficiently. *This statement is incorrect.*
 
• **Nerve cells are long to help in the conduction of impulses:** Nerve cells (neurons) have long extensions called axons that are adapted for transmitting electrical impulses over long distances. This structural adaptation supports their function. *This statement is correct.*
 
• **Cell shape is often related to its function:** The shape of a cell is closely linked to its function. For example, muscle cells are elongated to facilitate contraction, and epithelial cells are flat to form protective layers. *This statement is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Variation in cell size:**
 
 
• The size of cells varies greatly. For example, bacterial cells are typically 1-10 micrometers in size, while human egg cells can reach up to 100 micrometers.
 
• Some specialized cells, like neurons, can extend over a meter in length in large organisms.
 
 
 
• **Variation in cell shape:**
 
 
• Cell shapes are highly diverse and adapted to their functions. For instance:
 
 
• Red blood cells are disc-shaped to maximize surface area for oxygen exchange.
 
• Guard cells in plants are kidney-shaped to facilitate opening and closing of stomata.
 
• Nerve cells have branching structures for communication with other cells.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Structure and function correlation:**
 
 
• The relationship between structure and function is a fundamental principle in biology. For example:
 
 
• Muscle cells contain actin and myosin proteins for contraction.
 
• Leaf cells have chloroplasts to perform photosynthesis.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Cell diversity in organisms:**
 
 
• Multicellular organisms have specialized cells for different functions, such as blood cells for oxygen transport, immune cells for defense, and skin cells for protection.
 
• Unicellular organisms like amoebas perform all life processes within a single cell.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Examples of cell specialization:**
 
 
• Red blood cells lack nuclei to maximize space for hemoglobin, which transports oxygen.
 
• Root hair cells in plants have long extensions to increase surface area for water absorption.
 
 
 
• **Discovery of cells:**
 
 
• Cells were first discovered by **Robert Hooke** in **1665** when he observed cork under a microscope.
 
• The cell theory, proposed by **Schleiden** and **Schwann**, states that all living organisms are composed of cells, which are the basic unit of life.
 
 
 
• **Cell types:**
 
 
• Prokaryotic cells lack a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles (e.g., bacteria).
 
• Eukaryotic cells have a nucleus and specialized organelles (e.g., animal and plant cells).
